[Estimation](estimation.qmd) defines the accuracy of an estimator
at one sample size, through its bias, variance and population mean squared error.
This page asks two further questions:
what happens to an estimator as the sample size grows,
and how small can the variance of an unbiased estimator be?

- @CaseBerg01 [Sec. 7.3.2, pp. 334--341] covers best unbiased estimators and the Cramér--Rao bound.
- @rice2007mathematical [Sec. 8.5.2, pp. 274--278] covers large-sample theory for maximum likelihood estimators.
- @rice2007mathematical [Sec. 8.7, pp. 298--304] covers efficiency and the Cramér--Rao lower bound.
:::
